description: Matsumoto's eight-factor genus-two relation has six nonseparating and two separating twists. A one-boundary lift gives a section of square -1, and Hamada finds four disjoint such sections. Exact six-strand factor records are not yet encoded.

sections.Surface and conventions: The regular fiber is a genus-two surface. Capping the boundary of the framed relation gives a closed-surface identity of type (6,2).
sections.Derivation: Baykur-Korkmaz, Section 3.3, state Matsumoto's relation (t_B0 t_B1 t_B2 t_c)^2 = t_delta in the mapping class group of the genus-two surface with one boundary component.
sections.Braid factorization: The source curve diagram has not been converted into exact six-strand braid factors in this package. No checked interactive starting factorization is claimed yet.
sections.Planar mapping class diagrams: The cited papers depict the vanishing cycles and framed lifts; package support drawings remain to be constructed and checked.
sections.Standard mapping classes: Each repeated block has three nonseparating twists B0, B1, B2 and one separating twist c.
sections.Equivalences and transformations: Baykur-Korkmaz also describe a reverse-engineered (6,2) relation and identify it with a lift of Matsumoto's symmetric relation. A machine-checked conversion between their presentations is pending.
sections.Sections and multisections: The one-boundary relation gives one section of self-intersection -1. Hamada's Theorem 2 constructs four disjoint sections of self-intersection -1 for the genus-two Matsumoto-Cadavid-Korkmaz fibration. These are literature results, not boundary-framed checks by this package.
sections.References: Baykur-Korkmaz, arXiv:1510.00089, Section 3.3; Hamada, arXiv:1610.08458, Theorem 2.
